title: fixate-on completion verdict
description: The object a verifier must print on stdout. This is the wire contract of `verifierCommand` and of the project's own `completion-gate-json` make target; the plugin's parser is stricter than this schema in the ways noted in `description` at each constraint. Print one JSON object and nothing else.

schema_version.description: The contract version. Only 1 exists; a different number is a parse error, not a best-effort read.

task_id.description: The goal or task this verdict is about. Bounded at 256 characters.

state.description: The terminal state the verifier is willing to stand behind. COMPLETE: the agreed scope holds on the identified candidate. WORKING: not yet complete, and `outstanding` says what remains. BLOCKED: progress needs authority or an environment change the agent lacks. NEEDS_INPUT: progress needs a material decision from you. CANCELLED: an authorised actor ended the task.

candidate.description: Identity of the tree the verifier actually read — normally the git HEAD short sha. OPTIONAL, because a model acting as judge cannot compute it; an absent or empty value means 'not claimed' and the host stamps its own capture instead. A command verifier is held to it: an absent or disagreeing value is treated as a mismatch and the verdict is rejected. Bounded at 256 characters.

fingerprint.description: Identity of the whole tracked and untracked working tree the verifier read, as a digest. Same optionality and same bound as `candidate`.

outstanding.description: What remains. MUST be empty for COMPLETE and CANCELLED, and MUST hold at least one item for WORKING, BLOCKED and NEEDS_INPUT — the plugin rejects a state that contradicts its own list. At most 32 items, each 1 to 500 characters.

evidence.description: What the verifier actually observed, and the only thing that can settle a claim. MUST hold at least one item. At most 64 items, each 1 to 500 characters.
